raw_response:
I am 60 years old and have farmed these 7 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My bones know this soil. I have a wife at home and some children working in the city who send money, but the land is still my responsibility. I have a well for irrigation, though the water table drops every year and electricity is expensive.

Five mu will stay in the wheat-maize rotation as always. The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn — I used saved seed from an improved Jinmai variety that has done well on this plot. I will topdress nitrogen at jointing and irrigate three times: now at green-up, once at jointing, and a final grain-filling water if the sky doesn't give rain. Two pesticide sprays, one herbicide and one for rust or blight if the weather turns wet. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize using the no-till planter. Time is short — you must get the maize in quickly to have enough growing degree days before autumn cold. Similar fertilizer program, slightly less nitrogen because the soil is still warm and active. Two irrigations if July and August are dry. One herbicide at planting and watch for armyworms.

The 1.5 mu of watermelon is my cash crop. I will plough deeply and make high beds — melons need loose soil and good drainage. I buy expensive hybrid F1 seeds from the ag shop, but they give uniform fruit that the roadside buyers like. Watermelon needs potassium for sweetness, so I apply more potash fertilizer than on grain crops. Four careful irrigations — too much and the sugar drops, too little and the fruit is small. Three pesticide sprays because melons attract every pest and mildew in the county. I hope for 3,000 kg/mu.

Half a mu of cotton — I keep this partly from habit, partly because my wife can help pick it in autumn. I plant Bt hybrid cotton. Less fertilizer than grain crops. Two irrigations at flowering and boll stage. Even with Bt cotton, three pesticide applications for other insects. The yield should be around 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Why not more watermelon if it pays more? I am 60. Watermelon is backbreaking work — bending for planting, weeding, and harvest. One and a half mu is all my old waist can handle. The wheat and maize can be mostly mechanized. Cotton is easy to manage in a small plot. This balance gives me grain for household security and some cash for daily expenses.
